text:
marie: quick helm question — we're migrating a service from using envFrom: secretRef to explicit env + secretKeyRef, and seeing weird nil panics when ExternalSecret creates the secret slightly after deploy :thinking:

marie: current values.yaml snippet:
```yaml
secrets:
  oauthSecret: my-service-oauth
```

marie: deployment template uses envFrom which was convenient: 
```yaml
envFrom:
  - secretRef:
      name: {{ .Values.secrets.oauthSecret }}
```

marie: but some pods start before ExternalSecret populates and the app crashes when it expects API_TOKEN env var. Is explicit env with secretKeyRef the right move, or should we force helm to wait?

alex: I'd prefer explicit env with secretKeyRef for keys that are required by the app. envFrom is handy but fragile when secrets are created async or you need specific keys. Also easier to see which keys map to which vars.

alex: example template to safely render and fail fast if value missing (helm render-time check):
```yaml
# templates/_helpers.tpl
{{- define "requiredSecretName" -}}
{{- required (printf "missing values.secrets.%s" .) (index .Values.secrets .) -}}
{{- end -}}

# templates/deployment.yaml (snippet)
env:
  - name: API_TOKEN
    valueFrom:
      secretKeyRef:
        name: {{ required "values.secrets.oauthSecret is required" .Values.secrets.oauthSecret }}
        key: api_token
```

alex: that required() will cause helm to error on render/install if the value isn't set in values.yaml (not if the Secret resource is absent in the cluster). For cluster-side presence you can use lookup() but it's cluster-dependent at render time.

sam: another pattern is an init container that waits for the secret to exist before starting app (poll with kubectl or small curl to k8s API). It avoids helm-time errors but adds rollout wait time.

sam: example wait init container (super minimal):
```yaml
initContainers:
- name: wait-for-secret
  image: bitnami/kubectl:1.27
  command: ["/bin/sh","-c"]
  args: ["until kubectl get secret {{ .Values.secrets.oauthSecret }} >/dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 1; done"]
```

ravi: FWIW, if you need rotation and avoiding env leaks, consider mounting the secret with the projected CSI driver (k8s secrets as files). Then your app can read file and you get rotation without redeploy. That sidesteps envFrom vs secretKeyRef debate.

ravi: projected volume example: 
```yaml
volumes:
- name: oauth-secrets
  projected:
    sources:
      - secret:
          name: {{ .Values.secrets.oauthSecret }}
          items:
            - key: api_token
              path: api_token
```

marie: cool — two follow-ups: (1) I still want a short-term fix for the crash (explicit env + init container?), (2) any Helm templating gotchas when switching from envFrom to explicit env via values overrides in CI (we pass extra --set overrides)?

alex: for (1) explicit env + a short wait initContainer is safest for now. For (2) watch for quoting and yaml types when using --set. If the secret name contains dots or dashes, use --set-string or pass a values file. Also if your values may contain templating (like using tpl on values), ensure you call tpl in the template: 
```yaml
name: {{ tpl .Values.service.name $ }}
```

alex: last gotcha: if you switch from envFrom to explicit env in a chart consumer, the default values shape changes — update README and values.schema.json so CI linting catches it.

marie: thanks! I'll try explicit env + init container, and will update the values docs. tagging @ravi to consider CSI migration later. :+1:

deploy-bot: CI: lint/chart returned 1 warning: values.schema.json missing required property for secrets (chart-testing). See pipeline #842 for details.

marie: noted, I'll add schema and a tiny test to chart CI to ensure the secret name is present when chart is used in our overlays.

sam: ping me if you want a hand adding the init container helper, I can PR a small _helpers.tpl snippet.

marie: thanks all — will update thread after PR and test results.
